implementation_notes: Swift has no lock-per-object API for this problem; the platform idiom is confinement. Core Data confines a context (and the whole object graph it tracks) to a serial queue: the documentation says a context assumes the thread or queue that created it as owner and that access must be routed through perform(_:) or performAndWait(_:), so one context gives you one coarse lock over every member it holds. GRDB provides the same shape for SQLite with serialized writes inside dbQueue.write { db in ... }. Both replace per-member locks with a single serialization point; use the context/queue as the cluster's owner and keep cluster members in one context.
idiom_name: queue-confined NSManagedObjectContext / GRDB serialized writes over the cluster
pitfalls: The ownership rule is strict: passing the context or its objects to another queue (instead of passing the persistent container) is the classic Core Data crash and data-corruption source.

A context serializes access but does not prevent lost updates across contexts or processes - set automaticallyMergesChangesFromParent/mergePolicy deliberately, or use GRDB/SQL row locking for cross-process safety.
